title: Erdos #14: Unique representation sums and Sidon obstructions

problemStatement.formal: For A \subseteq \mathbb{N}, let U_A(N)=|[1,N] \setminus \mathrm{uniqueSums}(A)|. Study whether U_A(N) is forced near N^{1/2} and whether U_A(N)=o(\sqrt{N}) is possible.
problemStatement.plain: Erdos #14 studies how many integers fail to have a unique representation as a sum of two elements of A. The Lean file defines representation counts, unique sums, Sidon sets, and formal versions of the two open growth questions.
whyMatters: Links additive-combinatorics extremal questions with concrete representation-count definitions.
Clarifies why Sidon sets make all represented sums unique but are too sparse to resolve the density question alone.

proven: `IsSidon` and `sidon_all_unique` prove Sidon sets have all represented sums unique.
`sidon_size_bound` proves a square-root upper bound for Sidon sets in finite intervals.
`erdos_14a` and `erdos_14b` encode the two main growth questions.
open: The construction bounds are axiomatized as `erdos_upper_construction`, `erdos_lower_infinitely_often`, and `erdos_freud_finite`.
The current file notes that the quantified lower-bound formulation does not directly refute an o(sqrt(N)) example.
knownResults.goal: Separate theorem-backed Sidon/counting lemmas from the axiomatized Erdos construction bounds, then refine the growth-question formulations if needed.
